provenance.quote: PEEP optimization was achieved through a decremental PEEP test. Starting from 15 cmH2O, PEEP was reduced by 2 cmH2O increments every 2 min until reaching 5 cmH2O. At each PEEP level, end‐expiratory PL, oxygenation index, and respiratory system compliance (Crs) were documented. The optimal PEEP was identified as the level maintaining end‐expiratory PL between 0 and 2 cmH2O with the highest Crs.

method_verbatim.value: performing an occlusion test (the ratio of changes in Pes to airway pressure during occluded respiratory efforts should be 0.8–1.2)

position_verification.value: inserted through the nose to a depth of 40–45 cm and then withdrawn to 30–35 cm for optimal positioning in the mid‐esophagus, with position confirmation by chest X‐ray and the closed airway test; cardiac oscillations on the Pes tracing; reconfirmed after each position change and by chest X‐ray after the first proning session

recruitment_manoeuvre_detail.value: Lung recruitment maneuvers were performed when severe hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 ratio < 150 mmHg) or atelectasis (indicated by significant Crs decrease) occurred. The recruitment process involved a stepwise increase in PEEP to 30–40 cmH2O for 30–40 s, with continuous hemodynamic monitoring. Postrecruitment PEEP was set to the previously determined optimal level.

provenance.quote: Lung recruitment maneuvers were performed when severe hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 ratio < 150 mmHg) or atelectasis (indicated by significant Crs decrease) occurred.
provenance.location: Methods, 2.2.3, p. 2364

tidal_volume_target.value: 6 mL/kg predicted body weight initially, decreased to a minimum of 4 mL/kg PBW when end‐inspiratory PL exceeded 20 cmH2O

provenance.quote: For tidal volume adjustment, the initial setting was 6 mL/kg PBW, with subsequent modifications based on PL measurements. The target was to maintain end‐inspiratory PL below 20 cmH2O. When this threshold was exceeded, tidal volume was progressively decreased to a minimum of 4 mL/kg PBW.
provenance.location: Methods, 2.2.3, p. 2364

plateau_or_ptp_ceiling.value: end‐inspiratory PL < 20 cmH2O; ΔPL ≤ 12 cmH2O in EPM‐guided group; ΔP ≤ 15 cmH2O in both groups

other_co_interventions.value: Neuromuscular blockade (cisatracurium 0.15–0.2 mg/kg/h) per standardized protocol in both groups when indicated for dyssynchrony or PaO2/FiO2 < 150 mmHg for first 48 h; 45° semirecumbent position; prone positioning for PaO2/FiO2 < 150 mmHg (≥16 h sessions); conservative fluid management in both groups

provenance.quote: Neuromuscular blocking agents (cisatracurium, 0.15–0.2 mg/kg/h continuous infusion) were administered according to standardized protocol in both groups when indicated for patient–ventilator dyssynchrony or severe hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 < 150 mmHg) for the first 48 h of mechanical ventilation

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: BMI mean ~24.8 kg/m2, so non-obese. Timing: patients screened within 48h of mechanical ventilation, so early. Target: end-expiratory PL 0-2 cmH2O (positive range), absolute PES subtraction.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: No overlap with any COHORTS.md cluster. Single centre (Affiliated Anqing First People's Hospital of Anhui Medical University, Anqing, China), enrolment January–December 2023, ethics approval AFky2023010322, no trial registration number reported. None of the listed clusters (epvent1, epvent2, mannheim_boesing, mgh_lung_rescue, angers) involve a Chinese single-centre SAP-ARDS population; enrolment window postdates publication of talmor_2008, beitler_2019, fumagalli_2019, pirrone_2016, and boesing_2022.
unclear_items: citation.trial_registration: no trial registration number reported anywhere in the paper.
design.randomised: stated as randomized controlled trial with computer-generated randomization; no registration to verify.

comparator.comparator_types: the common initial protocol states 'Initial positive end‐expiratory pressure (PEEP) and FiO2 were adjusted according to the ARDSNet low PEEP/high FiO2 table' for both groups, while the conventional group protocol states 'PEEP and FiO2 adjustments followed the ARDSNet high PEEP/FiO2 table'; coded the conventional arm as ardsnet_high_peep_fio2_table per its dedicated protocol section, but the initial-phase low-PEEP table applies to both arms.
population.bmi: reported per arm in Table 1 only; cohort-level bmi left null rather than pooled.

feasibility.complications_explicitly_none: Table 7 records general complications (stress ulcer, arrhythmia, AKI, thrombosis) but the paper makes no statement about balloon-related complications specifically; left null.
outcomes: 12 h timepoint is mentioned in Methods ('baseline, 12, 24, 48, and 72 h') but no 12 h data appear in any table; 12 h data appear unreported.
intervention.timing: reference event is enrolment (screened within 48 h of mechanical ventilation), so timing_subgroup is unclear per codebook ruling.
extraction_flags.general_notes: Internal consistency concerns: several t values are identical across different rows/tables (e.g. t = 7.124 for both End‐inspiratory PL 72 h and Pplat 72 h; t = 0.432 for both BMI and VT baseline), and the abstract reports 'intensive care nit (ICU)' typo. The between-group difference in PaO2/FiO2 at 72 h is quoted as '73.41 ± 12.42 mmHg' in text, which matches 268.82 − 195.41 = 73.41. Fluid balance Day 1 (379 vs 542) equals cumulative 24 h row. No balloon placement success/failure or complication data specific to the catheter are reported. The multivariate model includes ΔPL (an post-treatment measurement) as a predictor of 28-day mortality, which the authors themselves acknowledge as a methodological caveat.
